data.title: Income Investors Should Know That Sakai Moving Service Co.,Ltd. (TSE:9039) Goes Ex-Dividend Soon
data.description:

The ex-dividend date is usually set to be two business days before the record date, which is the cut-off date on which you must be present on the company's books as a shareholder in order to receive the dividend. The ex-dividend date is important as the process of settlement involves at least two full business days. So if you miss that date, you would not show up on the company's books on the record date. Accordingly, Sakai Moving ServiceLtd investors that purchase the stock on or after the 29th of September will not receive the dividend, which will be paid on the 3rd of December.

Looking at the last 12 months of distributions, Sakai Moving ServiceLtd has a trailing yield of approximately 3.8% on its current stock price of JP¥3080.00. We love seeing companies pay a dividend, but it's also important to be sure that laying the golden eggs isn't going to kill our golden goose! We need to see whether the dividend is covered by earnings and if it's growing.

The license lets VEON and Square Group move from running Mukto Pay under a payment service provider license to operating a full digital bank inside Bangladesh. It shows the commercial program is still moving and that Rivian vehicles are embedded in a large logistics network. For the near term, the key watchpoint is whether those vans help drive steadier volume through existing plants.

That Amazon relationship also speaks to how Rivian balances risk. A concentrated lineup means success in midsize SUVs and commercial vans matters a lot. If Amazon volumes grow as expected and the software and services segment, including fleet tools, gains traction, that could support the push toward better margins. If not, investors are left relying more heavily on future platforms like R2 to carry the earnings narrative.

Rivian Automotive's current analyst model points to revenues of $20.8b and earnings of $736.7m by 2029, based on forecast yearly revenue growth of 52.3% and an earnings swing of about $3.9b from a loss of $3.2b today.

data.title: Manchester United (MANU) Climbed, But What Is Driving Attention Now?
data.description:

Recent trading tells a mixed story for Manchester United. The share price has climbed 2.20% over the past day and 5.01% across the last week, yet remains down 12.27% over 30 days and 8.64% over 90 days. This pullback follows the record revenue headline, enlarged loss and fresh guidance. Even so, the share price is still up 32.70% year to date, and the 1 year total shareholder return of 38.22%, alongside a 5 year total shareholder return of 9.52%, suggests long term holders have seen moderate gains while short term momentum has recently faded on earnings related uncertainty.
